title.en: Axisymmetric equilibrium map to Cartesian solver grid
title.zh: 轴对称平衡映射到笛卡尔求解网格

summary: Reconstruct the static magnetic field and poloidal flux of an axisymmetric equilibrium onto a Cartesian solver grid by tensor-product linear interpolation on the map's R-Z axes, clamping query points onto the closed map box and reporting where that clamping happened.

identity.relation: an axisymmetric equilibrium map in cylindrical coordinates and a rectilinear Cartesian solver grid to the static field, the poloidal flux, and the coverage of that grid by the map
identity.direction: equilibrium map arrays plus x_m, y_m, z_m -> magnetic_flux_density_t, poloidal_flux_wb_per_rad, covered_mask, radially_clamped_point_count, axially_clamped_point_count
identity.definition: Builds the radius and the axial coordinate of every Cartesian grid point, clamps each query coordinate onto the closed map box, evaluates the tensor-product linear interpolant of each map array at the clamped coordinates, splits the interpolated radial field into Cartesian transverse components, and marks the grid points that lay inside the closed map box.
identity.model: tensor-product (bilinear) interpolation of an axisymmetric map on a rectilinear R-Z grid, with independent clamping of each query coordinate onto the closed map box
identity.geometry: axisymmetric equilibrium map sampled on an R-Z grid, evaluated on a rectilinear Cartesian x-y-z solver grid
identity.coordinates: the map is cylindrical (r, z) and the target is Cartesian (x, y, z) with the axial coordinate shared; mesh built with C-order ij indexing over the target axes
identity.boundary: the relation is defined on the closed box spanned by the map axes; a query point outside that box is clamped onto the nearest box face rather than rejected or extrapolated, and the clamping is counted
assumptions: The equilibrium map is axisymmetric, so the map depends on radius and axial coordinate only and carries no toroidal mode structure.
The map axes are strictly increasing, so the enclosing interpolation cell of every clamped query coordinate is well defined.
The map arrays are finite, so the interpolation cannot be poisoned by a non-finite sample.
The radial field component is the poloidal field magnitude in the R-Z plane, so its Cartesian transverse split is br * (x, y) / r and is undefined on the axis.
The caller owns the equilibrium mapping and the grid; this relation retains no state and reads no file.

inputs.name: equilibrium
inputs.description: Caller-owned axisymmetric equilibrium mapping carrying r_m, z_m, psi_wb_per_rad, br_t, and bz_t.
inputs.constraints: Must be a mapping. r_m and z_m are finite strictly increasing 1D axes of at least five points; psi_wb_per_rad, br_t, and bz_t are finite [N_r, N_z] arrays on the map axes. No other entry is read, so the flux-surface classification parameters are not part of this relation.

inputs.name: x_m
inputs.constraints: Finite, one-dimensional, at least two points, strictly increasing.

inputs.name: y_m
inputs.constraints: Finite, one-dimensional, at least two points, strictly increasing.

inputs.name: z_m
inputs.description: Cartesian solver grid axial axis, shared with the map's axial coordinate.
inputs.constraints: Finite, one-dimensional, at least two points, strictly increasing.

outputs.name: magnetic_flux_density_t
outputs.description: Static magnetic field on the solver grid, with the field vector in the last axis.
outputs.constraints: Finite everywhere. The transverse pair is the interpolated radial field split as br * (x, y) / r and is set exactly to zero on the axis, where that split is undefined.

outputs.name: poloidal_flux_wb_per_rad
outputs.description: Poloidal flux per radian interpolated onto the solver grid.
outputs.constraints: Finite everywhere, and evaluated at the clamped query coordinates so that clamped points carry the box-face value.

outputs.name: covered_mask
outputs.description: Grid points that lay inside the closed box spanned by the map axes before clamping.
outputs.constraints: A point is covered when its radius is between the first and last map radial axis values and its axial coordinate is between the first and last map axial axis values. Because the map's radial axis is usually positive, the grid axis r = 0 is normally not covered.

outputs.name: radially_clamped_point_count
outputs.description: Number of grid points whose radius exceeded the outer map radius and was clamped onto it.
outputs.constraints: Counts only radii above the outer map radius, matching the retained relation; radii below the inner map radius are clamped as well but are not counted.

outputs.name: axially_clamped_point_count
outputs.description: Number of grid points whose axial coordinate lay outside the map axial axis and was clamped onto a face.
outputs.constraints: Counts points below the first and above the last map axial axis value.

preconditions: The equilibrium map is axisymmetric and finite on a strictly increasing R-Z grid of at least five points per axis.
The solver grid axes are finite and strictly increasing, and share the axial coordinate convention of the map.
The caller accepts that query points outside the map box are answered with the box-face value and reported through covered_mask.
supported: Any rectilinear Cartesian solver grid shape.
Grids that extend beyond the map box radially or axially, with the clamping reported.
An equilibrium map whose radial axis starts at zero, which makes the grid axis covered.
Any number of map samples at or above five per axis.
excluded: Extrapolation beyond the map box; the relation clamps instead.
Spline, conservative, or flux-surface-aligned interpolation; only tensor-product linear interpolation is defined here.
Flux-surface classification, PML framing, and PEC masking, which belong to the separate material-support relation.
Any unit conversion; the map arrays are taken in the caller's units.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError when equilibrium is not a mapping, when a required map entry is missing, when a map axis is not a finite strictly increasing 1D array of at least five points, when a map array does not have the [N_r, N_z] map shape or is not finite, or when a solver grid axis is not a finite strictly increasing 1D array of at least two points.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Raises ValueError if the assembled static field is not finite anywhere, which can only arise from an input the validation did not cover. There is no fallback interpolation method.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Not applicable; this relation is a single closed-form evaluation with no iteration or feedback.
failure_semantics.partial_results: Never returned; a rejected call produces no mapping.

provenance.lineage_summary: SciRel-owned split of the first of the two scientific relations that the retained coarse-CAD full-wave entry performed inside one operator. The retained operator also owned the closed-flux and magnetic-axis material-support classification and read the separatrix flux, the PML frame, and the PEC mask; this relation reads none of those, so the two are independent scientific identities and are proposed as separately reviewable assets. The retained docstring claimed that the two-stage interpolation ordering was part of the relation; the review measured that claim on a deliberately non-separable map and found that both orders produce the tensor-product bilinear interpolant to within float association, so the ordering is an implementation invariant rather than a discriminating choice, and the declared relation is the tensor-product form itself. The clamping is preserved exactly, including the retained asymmetry that only radii above the outer map radius are counted. The observation snapshot and the batch inventory are private review artifacts and are not part of the public contract. This asset is a sibling of the frozen real R-Z sampler scirel.geometry.sample_rectilinear_field, not a duplicate and not a successor of it: the frozen sampler takes a pair of 2-D coordinate meshes and returns a flat vector of real scalars at caller-chosen points, raising for a point outside its grid, whereas this relation takes an equilibrium mapping of named arrays with 1-D axes, returns the whole Cartesian solver grid including the cylindrical split and the poloidal flux, and clamps out-of-domain points onto the closed map box instead of failing closed. The candidate module deliberately does not import, shadow, or re-export the frozen sampler.

example.description: Reconstruct a synthetic equilibrium onto a 9x9x7 solver grid and check the shapes, the coverage count, and the on-axis transverse split.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.geometry import map_axisymmetric_equilibrium_to_cartesian_grid
r_axis = np.linspace(0.05, 1.0, 21)
z_axis = np.linspace(-0.5, 0.5, 21)
rr, zz = np.meshgrid(r_axis, z_axis, indexing='ij')
equilibrium = {
    'r_m': r_axis,
    'z_m': z_axis,
    'psi_wb_per_rad': 0.9 * rr + 0.1 * np.sin(2.0 * np.pi * zz),
    'br_t': 0.3 * rr - 0.1 * zz ** 2,
    'bz_t': 1.0 - 0.4 * rr ** 2,
}
result = map_axisymmetric_equilibrium_to_cartesian_grid(
    equilibrium,
    np.linspace(-0.5, 0.5, 9),
    np.linspace(-0.5, 0.5, 9),
    np.linspace(-0.4, 0.4, 7),
)
magnetic = result['magnetic_flux_density_t']
assert magnetic.shape == (9, 9, 7, 3)
assert result['poloidal_flux_wb_per_rad'].shape == (9, 9, 7)
assert result['covered_mask'].shape == (9, 9, 7)
assert result['covered_mask'].sum() == 560
assert result['radially_clamped_point_count'] == 0
assert result['axially_clamped_point_count'] == 0
assert np.isfinite(magnetic).all()
assert magnetic[4, 4, 3, 0] == 0.0 and magnetic[4, 4, 3, 1] == 0.0
assert magnetic[4, 4, 3, 2] != 0.0
example.expected: A finite [9,9,7,3] static field and a [9,9,7] poloidal flux, 560 covered grid points, no clamping, and an exactly zero transverse field on the grid axis.

scope: Agreement of the reconstruction with an independently built tensor-product bilinear interpolant on a deliberately non-separable map.
A measurement that the two-stage interpolation ordering is not discriminating on a rectilinear grid.
The coverage mask marking exactly the closed map box, including the inner-radius exclusion.
Both clamp counters, on a grid that extends beyond the map box on every face.
The Cartesian transverse split, including the exactly zero on-axis convention.
Fail-closed validation of the map axes, the map arrays, and the solver grid axes.
The absence of the classification parameters from this relation, by call and by import inspection.
Exact agreement with the retained reconstruction for the field, the flux, the coverage mask, and both counters.
verification.evidence_ceiling: Establishes that the declared tensor-product reconstruction reproduces the retained mapping relation and reports its clamping honestly. It does not establish that the equilibrium map itself is physically correct, nor that bilinear interpolation is adequate at any particular grid resolution, nor that the map's coordinate convention matches any specific device.
known_limitations: The interpolation is linear; a coarse map produces a piecewise-bilinear field with discontinuous derivatives across map cells.
Query points outside the map box silently receive the box-face value. The coverage mask and the clamp counters report this, but a caller that ignores them will not notice.
The retained asymmetry that only radii above the outer map radius are counted is preserved; radii below the inner map radius are clamped and counted by neither counter.
The relation assumes the axial coordinate is shared between the cylindrical map and the Cartesian grid; a target grid with a different axial origin would be mapped silently wrong.
Public distribution licensing remains pending a human decision.
